preview.pick: two mirror image forms of one agent differ in potency

served.stem: The passage presents all of the following as trouble for the lipid membrane theory EXCEPT
choices: a single degree of warming disorders a bilayer more than a clinical dose does
two mirror image forms of one agent differ in potency
pressure restores movement in an animal that has been anaesthetized
a soluble enzyme with no membrane is switched off in the order of clinical potency
some highly oil soluble compounds fail to keep an animal from moving
served.bankWhy: Pressure reversal is the one item on this list that the passage offers as support for the lipid theory, in paragraph 3, not as evidence against it. The other four all appear in paragraphs 4 through 6 as failures.

proof.quote: Warming a membrane by a single degree disorders the bilayer more than a clinical dose
the two differ in potency, one being measurably more effective
they do so in nearly the order of their clinical potency
ought to be powerful anaesthetics, and several of them are not
One observation appeared to seal the case.

passage.title: Why Anaesthesia Still Lacks an Explanation

distractorNotes: Paragraph 4 gives this as the first failure of the theory, since a mild fever would otherwise put a patient to sleep.
Paragraph 4 gives this as a failure of the theory, since oil cannot tell one mirror form from the other.
Paragraph 6 uses luciferase to show that the correlation never pointed at lipid in particular.
Paragraph 5 gives the non-immobilizers, whose oil solubility predicts a potency they do not have.

steps: Flip the job. All five are in the passage; you are hunting the one that is not trouble for the lipid theory.
Check off the trouble in paragraphs 4 to 6: warming, the mirror-image forms, the compounds that leave animals moving, luciferase.
Look where pressure sits: paragraph 3, as the observation that "appeared to seal the case". Support, not trouble.
